control_flow: followInTheDark: if the right light is below 60 % (in the dark), check the left light and the line tracker; else call avoidWalls.
avoidWalls: if the left light is below 70 %, turn away from a side wall (left wall: turn right, right wall: turn left), else call driveInTheDark; if bright, call driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if the left light is below 70 %, drive straight at 30 %; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: curve left on black, curve right on the floor.

likely_intent.description: Follow the black line, and keep following it through a dark tunnel too.

decision_points.condition: the right light is below 60 % (it is in the dark)

branches.outcome: the right light is below 60 %: the dark logic runs
the right light is 60 % or more: it goes on to avoidWalls

decision_points.condition: first: the left light is below 45 %; second: the line tracker reads above 95 %

branches.outcome: the left light is below 45 %: it curves left (15/35)

branches.reason: the line tracker reads above 95 % only in a narrow band just inside the tunnel
branches.outcome: the left light is 45 % or more and the line tracker reads above 95 %: it curves right (35/15)
the left light is below 70 %: it checks for side walls
the left light is 70 % or more: it goes on to stopAtWall

decision_points.condition: first: an obstacle on its left; second: an obstacle on its right

branches.outcome: an obstacle on its left: it turns right 20 degrees
no left obstacle but one on its right: it turns left 20 degrees
no side obstacle: it goes to driveInTheDark
the left light is below 70 %: it drives straight on at 30 %
the left light is 70 % or more: it goes on to stopAtWall
no obstacle ahead: it goes to followLine
the line tracker sees black: it curves left (10/40)

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left on black (10/40) and right on the floor (40/10).
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line in bright light, with nothing ahead.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black, then the floor, again and again.
scenarios.title: Follows the line in bright light
assumptions: You said 'too': following the line in bright light is already what you want.
The end of the line is where it should get to.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line to its end.

scenarios.coded_response: In the dark it curves left when the left light is below 45 %, curves right when the line tracker reads above 95 %, and otherwise drives on through avoidWalls.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line in bright light that runs into a straight tunnel.
scenarios.trigger: The right light drops below 60 % as it enters the tunnel.
scenarios.title: Follows the line through a dark tunnel
assumptions: The line runs through the tunnel to a goal at its far end.
The tunnel is wide enough to drive through.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line through the tunnel to its far end.

scenarios.coded_response: When the left light is below 70 % and the left sensor sees a wall, it turns right 20 degrees; when the right sensor sees one, it turns left 20 degrees.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is in dim light in a tunnel that bends, so one of its own walls comes in front of a side sensor.
scenarios.trigger: A side obstacle sensor sees the tunnel's wall.
scenarios.title: Turns away from the tunnel walls in the dark
assumptions: You didn't say this, but getting through the tunnel means not bumping into its walls.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It turns away from the wall and gets through the bend without bumping.

scenarios.coded_response: When the left light is 70 % or more and the front sensor sees a wall, it stops.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot follows a line in bright light, with a wall across the line ahead.
scenarios.trigger: The front obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall ahead
assumptions: You didn't say this, but stopping before a wall avoids bumping into it.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops before the wall without bumping into it.

uncertainties: Deep in a tunnel the left light is below 45 %, so the robot always curves left there; whether it really follows the line in the dark is uncertain.
The line tracker reading above 95 % inside a tunnel happens only in a narrow band, so the curve-right branch may be hard to trigger.
On a plain floor the robot curves right, so every test needs a line under it to get anywhere.
You didn't say how long the tunnel is or where the robot should end: the tests take the tunnel's far end as the goal.
